newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Insurer MMI sees higher 96/97 profit.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Insurer MMI sees higher 96/97 profit.

text.p: Insurance group MMI Ltd said on Thursday it was confident of achieving a significant rise in 1996/97 net profits due to strong investment returns and lower costs.

"Despite the commitment of significant capital to growth opportunities in Asia and the general development of our business in Australia, we remain confident that net profit will improve significantly in the current year assuming strong investment returns and the benefits of lower expense ratios," chairman John Curtis said in a speech prepared for the annual meeting.
MMI is about 48 percent owned by the Chamber of Manufactures of New South Wales, while German-based insurer and institutional investor Allianz AG Holding has a 14.5 percent stake.
Curtis said 1995/96 was a flat year for the insurer, with net profit rising six percent to A$35.0 million.

He said the company's strategic relationship with Allianz was developing, with a number of Asian-based ventures to be announced in the near future with efforts focussed on Vietnam, Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, and India.
MMI believed these activities would form a growing part of earnings in the medium term, Curtis said.

After the close of the 1995/96 year, MMI sold its 30.2 percent controlling stake in funds manager Pacific Mutual Australia to rival insurer Mercantile Mutual, a unit of Holland's Internationale Nederlanden Groep NV (ING).
Mercantile Mutual paid A$98 million for Pacific Mutual, or A$2.30 per share.
MMI shares were two cents lower at A$3.70 at 11.00 a.m. (0100 GMT).
